external_relations.target_title: smoke container checks only project files; it verifies almost no global install surface

source.description:
## PROBLEM

scripts/smoke-container/README.md calls itself a 'Pre/post-release gate' and says: 'Run it twice
around a coordinated release, once before publishing and once after. Both must PASS.'

Nothing else in the ecosystem says so. Measured 2026-07-27:

  ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-release.yaml   0 references
  docs/release.md                              0 references
  ~/.xtrm/skills/default/releasing/SKILL.md    0 references
  .github/                                     0 references
  package.json                                 0 references
  README.md, XTRM-GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md  0 references
  every global skill under ~/.xtrm/skills/default  0 references

The only mentions outside its own directory are 2 lines in
docs/design/audit-reconcile-v0724-epic-plan.md — a historical epic plan, not an operator runbook.

So the gate depends entirely on a human remembering a sentence in a README they would only read
if they were already in that directory.

## THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS THE OTHER SMOKE — do not confuse them

docs/release.md documents fresh-machine-smoke.yml, which IS a hard automated gate: publish.yml is
a 3-job DAG resolve_ref -> fresh_machine_smoke -> publish, and 'if smoke fails, publish never
starts'. That one is wired and enforced.

They test different things:
  fresh-machine-smoke.yml   live npm install + xt init -y + sp init — can a fresh user bootstrap
  smoke-container/verify.sh the GLOBAL install surface — claude/pi skill pointers, per-event hook
                            coverage, --new-instance, pi packages, and drift-repair

The bootstrap gate would not have caught bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.25 or xtrm-wiy5n.4.27. The container
gate is the one built to catch those, and it is the one nobody is told to run.

## WHY IT MATTERS NOW

Bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.32 just made this container a genuinely good gate: 7 fault injections each
prove one check, plus a drift-break-and-repair stage. A good gate that no runbook names is a gate
that will be skipped on the release after the person who built it stops paying attention.

## SUCCESS

- The release path names the container run, at the point where it must happen.
- Choose ONE owner for that instruction and put it there: docs/release.md, the releasing skill,
  or a node in the archon release workflow. Do not put it in three places that can drift apart.
- The instruction states the known pre-release exception, so an operator does not 'fix' a gate
  that is correctly reporting an unreleased fix.

## NON_GOALS

Making the container run automatically in CI. It needs docker and several minutes; wiring it into
every push is not the ask. The ask is that the RELEASE PATH names it.
